text: The next morning a boat came from the Sephora, and her captain, a thin, red whiskered man named Archbold, climbed aboard, saying that he had lost his chief mate. <break time="0.8s" /> Pretending to be a little hard of hearing, I made him repeat everything in a loud voice, for I wanted the hidden listener in my cabin to hear every word that passed between us. <break time="0.8s" /> Archbold told the story in his own way, never mentioning, as Leggatt had told me, that it was the mate, not he, whose order to set the foresail had saved the Sephora. <break time="0.8s" /> To show him that I had nothing to hide, I took him round the whole ship, opening even the door of my own stateroom, while my double stood silent in the inner corner. <break time="0.8s" /> Seven and thirty years he had been at sea, he declared, and never had he heard of such a thing happening in an English ship. <break time="0.8s" /> At last he left, unsatisfied, suggesting that the poor fellow must have drowned, and I watched his boat pull away with a relief so deep that my hands were trembling. <break time="0.8s" /> I knew well that, in the eyes of the law, Leggatt was a man who had taken a life, and that I, by hiding him, had become the secret sharer of his fate.
